title: Tokyo cash shut, Osaka open — Autumnal Equinox Day closes Silver Week on the US 5-Year and 2Y FRN auctions
source: EST: jpx.co.jp/english/corporate/about-jpx/calendar/index.html (Market Holidays, page's own 'Update : Feb. 06, 2026'), fetched direct 2026-09-15 (HTTP 200, 33,103 bytes) — the 2026 panel reads 'Sep. 23 (Wed.) Autumnal Equinox' under the standing rule 'JPX markets are closed on Saturdays, Sundays, national holidays, and on the dates indicated below.' SECOND PRIMARY, and the one that sets what actually trades: jpx.co.jp/english/derivatives/rules/holidaytrading/index.html (HTTP 200, 48,483 bytes, 'Update : Jun. 26, 2026') carries 'September 23 | Wed. | Autumnal Equinox Day | Open | Finalized' — derivatives trade, cash does not. THIRD PRIMARY: the exchange's own List_of_Finalized_Holiday_Trading_Days_E.xlsx (HTTP 200, 11,884 bytes, 78 rows) repeats 2026-09-23 as 'Open'. FOURTH, independent of JPX: Japan's Cabinet Office national-holiday file www8.cao.go.jp/chosei/shukujitsu/syukujitsu.csv (HTTP 200, 21,538 bytes, Shift-JIS, 1,067 holidays 1955-01-01 -> 2027-11-23), row 2026/9/23 秋分の日. All four re-fetched by this event's own initial research 2026-09-15, not inherited. The date is NOT derivable from statute — Autumnal Equinox Day tracks the astronomical equinox and is fixed each year by cabinet ordinance on the National Astronomical Observatory's determination, which is why it is read off the published ordinance above rather than computed. Stays estimate on the two standing counts the sibling jpx-market-closure entries already record, neither of them date doubt: market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for a securities exchange's own holiday calendar, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Checked 2026-09-15
notes: PROPOSED during the treasury-2y-note-2026-09-22 adjacency sweep (2026-09-15) as proposals/jpx-market-closure-2026-09-23.from-treasury-2y-note-2026-09-22.json; this canonical file was written by the never-assessed initial research of 2026-09-15 after reading that sole proposal, which stays where it is and is now shadowed. RESEARCHED 2026-09-15 (docs/research/events/jpx-market-closure-2026-09-23.md). CORRECTS the proposal's 'Tokyo dark' on the same primary the 09-21 sibling used — only the CASH equity market is shut; index futures/options and commodity futures trade 08:45-15:45 JST plus a 17:00-06:00 night session, so the US 13:00 ET 5-Year auction prints INSIDE an open Osaka session. Four findings this lane owns, none of them the sibling's. (1) STABILITY, not flippability: on the exchange's finalized file Autumnal Equinox Day has been 'Open' in every instance since JPX holiday trading launched — 2022-09-23 (the launch day itself was an Autumnal Equinox Day), 2024-09-23 substitute, 2025-09-23, 2026-09-23, and 2027-09-23 'Open | Scheduled'. That is 5/5, against Respect for the Aged Day's Open/Not Open/Not Open/Open/Not Open over the same window — so the sibling's 'JPX republishes it as Not Open' kill switch is materially weaker for 09-23 than for 09-21. (2) THE PRICE-LIMIT REFERENCE IS PINNED: JPX's Reference Prices rule states the holiday-trading reference price equals that of the night session of the business day before the holiday and is not updated during holiday trading, and that the day session of the business day after the holiday uses that same reference. So 2026-09-23 runs on a reference set Friday 2026-09-18 — and so does the 2026-09-24 cash reopen, six calendar days downstream of an FOMC (09-16), the BoJ (09-18), Japan CPI (09-18) and quarterly opex (09-18). Expanded limits set on a holiday session persist into the 09-24 day session. (3) HOLIDAY-SESSION VOLUME IS NOT PUBLISHED, which closes the 09-21 sibling's stated highest-value open item: JPX's Handling of Publication rule reads 'Trading volume and other statistics ... during holiday trading will be published after aggregated with those of the night session of the business day before the holiday. We will not publish those statistics separately just for the holiday trading day.' All three Silver Week sessions share Friday 09-18's trading day, so the block's volume is one aggregated figure — unfetchable by construction, not merely unfetched. (4) THE AUCTION ATTRIBUTION HAS n=0 FOR THIS TENOR. Fiscal Data auctions_query (4,105 rows since 2016, pulled direct 2026-09-15, shares over competitive accepted): across the 16 Treasury auctions ever held on a September equinox/sandwich holiday, NO 5-Year note and NO 2-Year FRN appears — the coupon auctions are three 2-Year notes (2018-09-24, 2020-09-22, 2025-09-23) and two 10-Year TIPS reopenings (2016-09-22, 2021-09-23); everything else is bills. On any Japanese national holiday the 5-Year has n=2 (2020-11-23 indirect 56.46%, 2022-02-23 67.81%) and the 2Y FRN n=2 (2021-11-23, 2022-02-23). So the temptation to explain the 5-Year's soft 2026-08-26 indirect (61.51% vs a 63.65% prior-11 mean) with 'Tokyo was shut' rests on zero precedent, not on a weak one. The aggregate null holds on this lane's own recomputation, on strictly nominal note/bond auctions (TIPS and FRNs excluded): indirect 60.88% dark (n=29) vs 61.77% open (n=821), Welch t=-0.468; dealer 21.46/21.67, t=-0.091; cover 2.500/2.507, t=-0.211. Two cuts of ~15 clear |t|=2 and both sit on tiny arms — 2-Year notes' bid-to-cover 2.530 (n=9) vs 2.653 (n=113), t=-2.459, and 10-Year dealer takedown on n=2, t=-3.445 — which is what a multiple-comparison artifact looks like; registered, not claimed. TWO METHODOLOGICAL TRAPS THIS LANE HIT AND THE NEXT ONE SHOULD NOT: Fiscal Data's original_security_term is the term of the ORIGINAL issue, not of the auction (2026-01-26 reads '5-Year' for what security_term calls a 2-Year reopening), and 5-Year/10-Year TIPS carry security_type 'Note', so a naive 5-Year filter picks up both. Filter on original_security_term AND security_term AND inflation_index_security='No' AND floating_rate='No'. This is also why base rates here read below the 09-21 sibling's 63.35%/61.88% — its 1,109-auction pool includes the 130 FRNs (indirect 54.5%, dealer 43.2%) and the TIPS; neither figure is wrong, the bases differ. The sibling's 5Y bid-to-cover kill threshold (below 2.28) is unaffected — 2.28 is the last-12 minimum on either basis; only its stated 2.57 maximum is a TIPS reopening rather than a nominal 5-Year. Impact low and unmoved: no Japan-listed symbol is tracked here, symbols is empty, and a grep of docs/plans/trade-playbooks.md and docs/research/multi-symbol-sweep.md for 'holiday|jpx|tokyo|nikkei|closure|equinox|osaka' returns zero hits in both, run 2026-09-15. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action.
